body:
## Summary

`exclude-newer-package = { <name> = false }` (the #16854 sentinel) is the right tool for exempting first-party packages from a dependency cooldown — but in a monorepo with many uv workspaces there is currently no way to define the exemption list once. It must be duplicated verbatim into every workspace's `[tool.uv]`, because:

- there is no environment-variable form (`UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER` exists; `UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER_PACKAGE` does not),
- TOML has no include mechanism and `[tool.uv]` has no way to reference an external file,
- each workspace root is its own configuration root — a `uv.toml`/`pyproject.toml` at the repository root above several workspace roots is not consulted when resolving inside them (only user-/system-level config merges in, which is machine state rather than repo state).

## Our concrete case

A monorepo with ~37 `[tool.uv]` manifests across ~10 separate workspaces enforces `exclude-newer = "7 days"` as a supply-chain cooldown. First-party packages publish to an internal index (pypiserver) that serves no PEP 700 `upload-time`, so without exemptions an active cooldown filters every internal package to zero versions; and even with upload-time metadata, a cooldown would embargo fresh internal releases. The fix is `exclude-newer-package: { <each internal name> = false }` — ~39 names — which today means an identical ~40-line table copied into all 37 manifests, held in sync by a repo-specific CI test that re-derives the list from the tree's `[project].name` inventory.

That works, but every project with this shape will end up writing the same derive-and-assert machinery.

## Ask (any one of these would collapse the duplication)

1. **File reference**: e.g. `exclude-newer-package-file = "path.toml"` (analogous to how other tools allow list externalization), resolved relative to the config file that declares it.
2. **Environment form**: `UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER_PACKAGE="pkg1=false,pkg2=false"` — this would also serve CLI-driven paths (containers, CI steps) that currently need the repeated `--exclude-newer-package` flag.
3. **Repo-level config**: an opt-in configuration file above workspace roots that project config merges with (project taking precedence), so multi-workspace repositories can state resolution policy once.

Related but distinct: #20788 (globs) would shrink the table for prefix-disciplined names but doesn't centralize it, and legacy unprefixed names remain enumerated; #19864 is about pin-based bypass semantics, not configuration sharing.

Happy to provide more detail on the monorepo layout if useful.
title: Allow sharing exclude-newer-package across workspaces: file reference, env var, or repo-level config
